name: desertres
note: The Desert Resort pack on Meshy, the seventh of the US golf courses' landscapes (7 November 2026): Shadow Creek, TPC Summerlin, PGA West. Afghan and Aleppo pines, weeping willow, olive, date palm and Mexican fan palm; its velvet mesquite is Desert Target's. Form from the owner's Shadow Creek and Summerlin photographs, tall open dark pines over green turf, and the reference photographs of Palm Desert, whose fan palms are very tall and thin with tiny heads. Sizes PLACED. The willow is a dome of overlapping fluffy tufts with a soft low fringe: long solid masses came out as sausages, and stepped chains of tufts as cones, which the owner turned down. The owner also turned down wind-swept shapes and a strong S in a trunk (7 November). No cypress here, the owner's rule (5 November). `seasons` are PLACED. Shipped in vendor/blender-meshy_desertres as DrAfghan, DrAleppo, DrWillow, DrOlive, DrDate, DrFan, because the hand-built models hold the plain names. The African sumac (the owner, 9 November 2026: the hand-built one "doesn't look like anything we built") added from reference photographs of cultivated trees in Tempe, Berkeley and Clovis and wild ones in Gauteng (Wikimedia Commons; docs/studies/us-golf-courses/photos/Desert Resort/african-sumac): a short dark trunk forking low into crooked limbs, an open rounded crown as wide as tall or wider, fine willow-like leaves drooping at the tips. Sizes PLACED inside species.js africansumac.
style: Stylised cartoon game art in soft, flat painted colour. Simple clean shapes with a gentle gradient: darker near the trunk and under each bough, lighter toward the tips. Matte, muted natural palette. No photographic detail, no photo bark, no noise, no speckle, no hard shadows, no highlights, no shine, no ink outlines, no text.
view: One view only, seen from the side at eye level, the whole plant in frame from foot to tip with a margin around it, centred, on a plain white background, in even soft light, with no cast shadow.
